title: Non-productive "You can't go that way" streak from unmarked futile exits
root_cause_hypothesis: Decision logic originates the bad data: determine_next_action keeps selecting "down"/"out" exits because _mark_edge_futile only fires when _compute_utility returns "futile", but "You can't go that way." is not in the hard_failure_patterns list, so these hard-failing moves are never classified futile and the same Unknown edges are re-offered.
change_summary: Add "you can'?t go that way" (and the equivalent "can'?t go in that direction") to the hard_failure_patterns so a rejected movement is classified as util=futile. Once _compute_utility returns "futile" for a direction action, the existing _mark_edge_futile path fires and the Unknown edge is permanently skipped in future unknown-exit scans, breaking the streak at its origin. This targets the pattern config that feeds decision_logic rather than adding a downstream guard.
acceptance_criteria: In a future run log, after a 'You can't go that way.' response to a direction, the same (room, direction) edge shows data.futile=true and is not re-selected on subsequent steps
The log entry for a 'You can't go that way.' movement records utility='futile' rather than 'informative'
No repeated 4-action same-direction streak against 'You can't go that way.' appears in step ranges of subsequent runs
risk_notes: The existing default hard_failure_pattern r"you can'?t" already matches "You can't go that way." at the game_config default level — but the Knight Orc run uses configs/knight_orc.json overrides, which may supply a narrower hard_failure_patterns list that omits it. Confirm the loaded config actually matches this phrase before assuming a code change is needed; if the default is in force the real gap is elsewhere (e.g. these edges are being re-added by update_graph after being pruned). Ensure the new pattern is genuinely permanent (a true "no exit that way") and not a state-dependent blockage, so we don't persist a futile edge that later opens — Knight Orc's "You can't go that way." is a permanent no-exit message, so this is safe.
fixed_in: PR TBD — the risk_notes above were right to be suspicious: verified against the actual loaded config that "you can'?t" IS present and DOES match "You can't go that way." (confirmed via game_config.hard_failure_pattern.search), and the run log shows util=futile was in fact computed on nearly every "out"/"down" attempt. The real gap was in agent.py, not config: "in"/"out" were missing from the _DIRECTIONS set, so process_agent_step's `if utility == "futile" and action_taken in _DIRECTIONS: _mark_edge_futile(...)` guard silently skipped them — "down" (a real cardinal direction) got marked futile correctly and was never retried, while "out" kept being re-offered indefinitely. Added "in"/"out" to _DIRECTIONS (same fix as P005 — one root cause, two anomaly reports from the same run). No config/pattern change needed.
